correctness.rationale: The Fock radial basis calculation gives exactly the Gamma-shell eigenvalues. For each k the Thue–Morse block product turns the signed sum into sampled k-fold differences. Sampling and translation integrals bound these by k-th and (k+1)-st Gamma derivatives, whose exact Laguerre Rodrigues L1 bounds give the claimed certificate for every n≥k+1. Optimizing k proves squared-log decay, hence summable eigenvalue powers. The exact Laplace product and absolute summability show trace zero, while q0>0 proves nonzero and opposite signs. checker.py replayed successfully with 120 finite assertions; its tests are supplementary.

originality.rationale: Prouhet identities are classical and the Gamma eigenvalue formula is established. The candidate new content is their application to a nondecaying, binary infinite radial shell mask yielding a nonasymptotic factorial eigenvalue bound, superpolynomial compactness of the half-identity perturbation, and exact zero trace. The closest inspected papers state different, strictly weaker, or non-implying results; historical priority is provisional.
residual_risks: A previously published general automatic-sequence spectral smoothing theorem, under another vocabulary, could imply a part or all of the present specialized result.

The selected first-public date is that of the focal Gaussian localization literature (2019), not a claim that the classical Thue–Morse sequence was first known then.

value.rationale: A natural automatic binary shell mask of infinite area has no pointwise decay, yet its Fock concentration operator is a trace-neutral perturbation of one-half identity in all Schatten ideals, with an explicit all-index factorial bound. This is a structural spectral homogenization of an infinite, nonperiodic observation domain; its sharp mechanism depends on Prouhet moment cancellation. The precise fact informs how nondecaying symbolic geometry can be spectrally invisible at high Hermite energy and is not a finite enumeration.
